Subject: Proposal: 36-month commitment + locked-rate request

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week. EdgeHealth is prepared to move forward with a 36-month commitment across 3 product routes (generation, embedding, rerank) if we can secure a locked rate for the duration and a cap on annual uplift tied to CPI (+2% max). We need predictable unit economics for budgeting and a single PO per year.

Attached is a short procurement summary and our SOW. Key asks:
- 36-month locked rate for list generation model (usage tiers attached)
- uplift cap = CPI + 2% (floor 0%)
- renewal protection: right to renew at the then-current locked rate with 60 day notice

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate this? We are targeting a decision by the end of the month.

Regards,
Sara

Sara —

Appreciate the clear asks and the SOW. Short answer: we can get very close, but the pricing concession you're requesting (locked-rate for 36 months + uplift cap) is beyond our standard auto-approved discount bands. I’ve looped in Deal Desk and Sales Ops to quantify impact and surface for exec approval.

What I recommend as a structure to speed this:
- Locked unit rate for 36 months with an annual CPI+2% cap (no floor below 0%)
- Minimum ARR commitment floor of $1.2M annually (EdgeHealth expects ~1.5M)
- Auto-rollback if usage drops below 65% of forecast for two consecutive quarters

If Deal Desk confirms the concession puts us outside delegated signoff, I’ll ask for expedited executive approval this week so you can get terms in the PO.

Aditya

- Proposed ARR floor mitigates tail risk; recommended to set floor at $1.25M/yr and require quarterly usage reporting.

Team —

Thanks for the analysis, Karthik. Approve executive concession with the following binding guardrails:
1) ARR floor = $1.25M/yr, measured at contract signature and trued up quarterly.
2) Auto-rollback: if billed usage < 65% of forecast for any two consecutive quarters, revert to standard list rates for subsequent quarter.
3) Renewal protection: EdgeHealth can elect to renew at the then-applicable locked rate only if they provide 60 days' notice and are not in breach of the usage covenant.
4) Include a 2% goodwill credit at renewal if annual consumption exceeds 110% of forecast.

Aditya — please get legal to pull the locked-rate language into the SOW and route a short exec approval letter for Lauren to sign. Loop me on the DocuSign. We want to keep this moving; procurement is timeboxed.

Marissa
